subject.scope: public unauthenticated chart and terminal entry

findings.claim: The public chart issues two overlapping GET requests to the same user-settings endpoint from separate Fetch and XHR frontend paths and receives byte-identical successful responses.
causal_chain: modern chart-theoretical-info bundle requests user settings with Fetch
legacy chart_grid restore path requests the same settings with XHR
the browser and server perform redundant work
findings.human_impact: Confirmed unnecessary network and backend work on public chart startup. No visible chart corruption, stale quote, account impact, or trading-decision impact was established.
findings.repair: Create one shared settings-loading owner or promise/cache and let both chart consumers use the same result. Add a regression assertion that one navigation produces at most one in-flight GET for the endpoint.

findings.claim: The public chart or terminal login leaves a first-party WebSocket alive after reload or navigation-away.
findings.reason: Neither public surface naturally opened a first-party Tradernet WebSocket during the bounded lifecycle run. Absence of a testable transport cannot support a zombie-connection claim.

findings.claim: The chart keeps stale market information visible during a transport outage without a freshness indicator.
findings.required_evidence: Repeat during an active market session with a naturally updating quote source, prove updates stop during offline mode, preserve timestamped visible state, and prove recovery after reconnect.

findings.claim: The natural 33,404-byte settings POST on public chart startup is unnecessary or mutates state incorrectly.
findings.required_evidence: Establish product intent, session state, payload semantics, repeated-navigation behavior, and measurable user or backend cost before assigning a defect. Raw request bodies were not retained.

pythia.rule: Only the 3-of-3 overlapping, successful, byte-identical duplicate request crosses the confirmation boundary.

selected_path: modern Fetch settings loader and legacy XHR restore loader coexist
two overlapping requests target the same endpoint
responses are byte-identical in 3 of 3 fresh contexts
consolidate settings ownership and add one-in-flight regression guard
cml.shared_root_cause_scope: The dual-loader cause is supported for this endpoint only and is not asserted as the root cause of other Tradernet mobile or runtime findings.

ls.control_assessment: The confirmed issue wastes startup resources but does not currently demonstrate misleading market state or loss of user control.

liminaldb.supersession: A future market-open lifecycle run may supersede the stale-state and zombie-transport uncertainty but cannot alter this exact evidence record.
